messages:
ashwin: quick heads-up — started seeing a p50 regression (~12%) on qwen-34b int4+fp8 profile after yesterday's kernel-priority tweak. mostly on long prefix workloads (>1024 tokens).

maria (ml-infra): ugh, thanks. can you paste a short profile/sample trace?

ashwin: pasted below — this is a 1h perf run against canary. note the jump when batcher switches kernels mid-seq and kv hit-rate drops.

ashwin: ```
# summary (canary-run 2026-03-16T14:02Z)
model: qwen-34b
profile: int4-primary, fp8-fallback enabled
workload: long_prefix_chat (seq 1500 avg)
baseline p50: 88ms tok
canary p50: 99ms tok
kv cache hit-rate baseline: 86%
kv cache hit-rate canary: 67%
batch sizes: baseline avg 4.1 -> canary avg 3.6
kernel swap events: 18k
kv-eviction spikes coincide with kernel-swap windows
```

kai: interesting — kernel-priority tweak bumped INT4 kernels above fp8 for memory util reasons, which reduced memory fragmentation normally, but if int4 kernel path temporarily uses slightly more scratch for kv-copy, we could be triggering spill/eviction.

sophie: any flame graphs or per-kernel counters? suspect KV latency + cache churn is the culprit.

perf-bot: automated snapshot attached: perf_snapshot_2073456789.tar.gz (uploaded) — heatmap shows >x2 stall on kv-load during kernel-switch windows.

maria (ml-infra): can you share the exact patch that rolled? i'll revert locally for a canary.

ashwin: patch diff:```
- kernel_priority: [fp8_fast, int4_lowmem, int8_balanced]
+ kernel_priority: [int4_lowmem, fp8_fast, int8_balanced]
```

kai: that explains it. ordering change was meant to favor lower mem footprints, but we didn't account for transient scratch/kvcopy patterns under long prefixes. The batcher chooses smaller batches when kernel swap happens -> reduced batching efficiency -> higher p50.

sophie: quick mitigation: make batcher sticky to kernel choice for a request (don't re-evaluate mid-seq), or prefer kernel with better kv-behavior for requests with >1k prefix. Propose config toggle: ```
batcher: {
  kernel_affinity: ON, 
  reassess_interval: never_mid_sequence,
  kernel_preference_by_prefix_length: [{min_prefix: 1024, prefer: fp8_fast}]
}
```

maria (ml-infra): i can roll a canary with kernel_affinity=ON + revert priority change. will run cluster-wide perf job.

perf-bot: triggered canary job 2073456901 — will report once 30m completes.

ashwin: initial manual test (single node) with kernel_affinity=ON shows p50 back to 90ms and kv-hit 84%. batch size recovered to 4.0.

kai: sounds promising. longer-term: we should teach kernel-selection heuristic to account for two metrics: (1) steady-state memory footprint, (2) kv-cache access pattern cost. right now priority is single-dim memory.

sophie: also flagging this as potential regression for mixed-precision profiles when sequence length distribution has heavy tail. we should add an eval test: long-prefix tails + randomized kernel-priority to catch this.

maria (ml-infra): action items i captured: 1) revert kernel-priority for qwen-34b canary (maria) 2) enable batcher.kernel_affinity for affected models (maria) 3) add long-prefix perf regression test to CI (ashwin) 4) add kv-metrics to kernel selector scoring (kai) 5) postmortem if canary shows improvement (sophie).

ashwin: yup. i'll open a tiny repro with synthetic prefix patterns and attach to the ticket. note: this also surfaces that our calibrations for int4 were ignoring kvcopy scratch usage during multihead attention — we should add a small microbench to capture scratch high-water marks during calibration.

kai: good call. that microbench should run across fp8/int4 kernels and emit a per-layer scratch histogram. can be part of model onboarding.

perf-bot: canary finished: p50 returned to 89ms, kv-hit 85%, batch size 4.05. marking canary=success.

sophie: great. let's still keep the prioritization change off for now until we implement kernel-scoring. thanks all :thumbsup:

ashwin: thanks — will follow up with the repro and CI test PR today.
